system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review — Project Kestrel.** Recommendations below are proposed negotiating positions, not agreed terms. This review relies on the supplied extracts; the underlying DD documents and full SPA have not been independently reviewed.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery for general warranties, without consuming separate protection for title, tax, specific indemnities or fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and negotiated security; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000** individually and **AUD 250,000** collectively; only the excess over the basket is recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; application confined to general warranties. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, aggregating related claims; the current deductible structure materially erodes recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with distinct periods for other categories and workable notice requirements. | **Require 24 months and preserve timely notified claims until resolved**; 18 months may not expose issues across two reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limit. | Separate protection covering capacity, ownership, all issued shares and freedom from encumbrances. | **Require a separate 100%-of-price cap, no thresholds and a seven-year contractual claim period**, appropriately documented; ownership risk is not ordinary operating risk. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | All-Claims limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance language; no express fraud protection identified. | Express preservation of fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation claims and non-excludable statutory rights. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions**, covering relevant Seller representatives; boilerplate must not shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the exception, linked to relevant warranties. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure; require specific, fairly disclosed exceptions and a frozen indexed disclosure set**; document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for knowledge of the Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from records. | No constructive, imputed or adviser knowledge exclusion; preferably no knowledge defence at all. | **Delete; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal leads of the relevant breach at signing**, with Seller bearing proof; discoverability is not informed acceptance of risk. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, described as “addressed”. | Effective consent satisfying clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable amendments, charges or termination rights. | **Make satisfactory, effective consent a Buyer-waivable condition precedent, with evidence of associated conditions being met**; final consent is absent and approximately 30% of revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release provided after Completion. | Repayment and effective discharge of all relevant security and guarantees at Completion, reflected in debt-free/cash-free pricing. | **Require a lender payout letter and simultaneous repayment/release mechanics, funded through Seller proceeds without double counting**; the Buyer must not complete with residual secured debt exposure. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-cost treatment unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable employer on-costs, with payment and price treatment explicit. | **Include bonuses plus verified on-costs as Seller-funded completion deductions or debt-like items, backed by an indemnity**; omission risks shifting transaction costs onto the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** is recorded open, without independent verification. | Evidence of cleared payment and effective IP ownership, plus protection against historic title defects and resulting claims. | **Require payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment before Completion; broaden the indemnity beyond the fee to resulting title, infringement and remediation losses**; paying an invoice alone may not establish clean IP ownership. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and unlikely material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, preservation/containment, legally required notifications and allocation of pre-Completion incident costs to Seller. | **Require investigation deliverables, interim covenants and a specific indemnity, with security proportionate to findings**; neither a confirmed breach nor immateriality is established. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, treated as ordinary-course costs. | Assess the related commitments together, including timing, necessity, termination rights and accounting treatment. | **Reserve agreement pending DD-008/DD-011 review; require Buyer approval for non-ordinary commitments and appropriate price treatment if debt-like or Seller leakage**; neither automatic deduction nor ordinary-course treatment is supported yet. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims. | Expressly differentiated regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, debt/price obligations and fraud. | **Rewrite the cross-cutting provisions and specify each category’s cap, thresholds, period and remedy treatment**; otherwise general boilerplate can defeat separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership chain, encumbrances, options and transfer restrictions, with valid transfer deliverables. | **Reconcile corporate records, certificates and issuance/transfer history; conduct relevant searches and obtain releases and completion registrations**; the share register is evidence, not complete title diligence. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion liabilities, longer tax protection and appropriately robust IP ownership and infringement protections. | **Expressly reopen both: seek seven-year tax protection with tailored limits, and separately negotiate IP scope, duration and cap alongside Ironquay protection**; Seller’s assertion of settlement does not resolve materially different risks. |

**Priority completion gates:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment/security releases, clean share-title deliverables and satisfactory Ironquay ownership evidence. Keep these distinct from post-Completion damages remedies.
=== END ADVICE ===
